feat(plugins): generic platform state + world-event re-probe (install-order epic) (#1808)

title: v0.14.0
featureLines: Linux window dragging is smoother and more precise, from displayxr-common v2.25.0:
**Wayland move-sync support** — when the runtime move-syncs the window, the app no longer applies its own drag lattice, so the two never fight.
**Right-button drag ends on release** — releasing the right mouse button now reliably ends a drag.
**X11 drag steps land exactly** — each drag step lands on its intended position with no drift.
**X11 header-bar double-click maximises** the window.

title: v0.10.0
featureLines: Window dragging on Linux is smoother and more precise, from the displayxr-common v2.25.0 repin:
**Wayland move-sync support**: when the runtime move-syncs the window, the app no longer applies its own drag lattice, so the window tracks the pointer directly.
**Right-button drag ends on release**: a right-button window drag now stops as soon as the button is released.
**Exact X11 drag steps**: each drag step on X11 lands exactly where it was computed.
**X11 header-bar double-click maximise**: double-clicking the header bar on X11 maximises or restores the window.

title: v1.11.0
featureLines: Linux window dragging is smoother and more precise, from the displayxr-common v2.25.0 window fixes:

title: DisplayXR Shell v2.3.0
featureLines: The shell installer now refuses to install against a runtime it cannot work with. It
requires **DisplayXR Runtime >= 2.16.0** and hard-aborts below that floor instead of
installing a shell that would fail at startup — and every installer modal is now
`IfSilent`-guarded, so unattended / bundle installs never stall on a dialog nobody can
see. Recommended pairing for this release: **runtime v2.17.1**.
Installer: hard runtime-version floor `MIN_RUNTIME_VERSION=2.16.0`, derived from the
pinned extension headers rather than hand-typed, with all modals `IfSilent`-guarded
so silent installs stay silent (#115, #113)

title: DisplayXR Shell v2.2.0
featureLines: Voice control works again. A missing dependency ceiling let a new major of the
`mcp` Python package into the shipped voice runtime, where it wedged during
session initialization — voice appeared to start and then silently did nothing,
leaving an empty log behind. The runtime is now pinned to the major we test, and
a wedged voice process says so (in the log, and as a toast) instead of failing
invisibly. Voice reaches `[realtime] session ready` and push-to-talk arms.

title: DisplayXR Unity Samples v2.1.0
featureLines: **desktop-avatar: `TigerFaceViewer`** (#9) — a head-tracked billboard that turns to
face the viewer, plus an A/B probe for comparing tracked vs. static framing. Built on
the plugin's `DisplayXRProvider.TryGetViewerHead` / `TryGetViewerEyes` API
(displayxr-unity#236), which is the supported way to read the tracked viewer position;
the earlier `Camera.GetStereoViewMatrix` approach returned the same mono matrix for
both eyes under the display provider and silently never tracked.
**desktop-avatar: opt-in 3D-zone edge feather** (#10) — requests a soft composite edge
on the avatar's 3D zone via the plugin's new `SetZoneFeather` API
